clue.text: Picked up important little bird

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: something important is key; wee is Scottish and informal for little

explanation.surface: Someone hears about a significant small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: It's a good mark? Confusingly, the opposite

indicators.note: confusingly means the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether something is a mark of merit, answered by its reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to 'a good mark': the answer is the opposite of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, the reverse of a badge of honour.

clue.text: Pop diva wearing fake sable stands outside

indicators.note: the jumbled sable is worn around the diva, so it goes outside her
fake means the letters of sable are made into something false, rearranged

parts.note: Cher is the American pop diva

explanation.surface: A singer in imitation fur stands outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands outside' looks like wordplay for a container, but it is the definition: American open-air spectator seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleachers are tiered uncovered seats at an American sports ground, open-air spectator stands.

clue.text: Gangster supports criminal circle of white-collar workers?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter sits beneath, so AL comes after
criminal means the letters of circle are bent out of shape

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster, giving AL

explanation.surface: A mobster backs a criminal ring of office workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns CIRCLE into CLERIC; the question mark admits that 'of white-collar workers' stretches the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical work is office work done by clerks, the classic white-collar employees.

clue.text: Mourinho's sacked after drawing in a friendly

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling the a inside the jumbled letters
sacked suggests something ransacked, its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: José Mourinho is fired after his team draws a friendly match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges MOURINHOS into HRMONIOUS, which takes in A after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonious relations are amicable and free of discord, a near synonym.

clue.text: Snipping custom thing for sale over in city

parts.note: a bris is the Jewish circumcision ceremony, a custom involving snipping

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lot is an item for sale at auction

explanation.surface: A tailoring shop's cut-price custom-made goods are in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LOT to TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large port city in south-west England, the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: 6A engineer's letter once held by British Library

indicators.note: held by means the letter sits inside the library's abbreviation

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for the British Library
a rune is a letter of an old Germanic alphabet, used in former times

explanation.surface: An old letter written by a famous engineer is kept in the national library.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed Bristol's Clifton Suspension Bridge and the SS Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel was the Victorian engineer whose landmark works define the city of Bristol.

clue.text: Recall man with a dog modelled one time for 6A films

indicators.note: modelled means the letters are shaped anew, like plasticine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Remember a man and his dog who were once made from clay for animated films.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallace and Gromit are made by Aardman Animations, based in Bristol; the surface describes the films themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The claymation series featuring an inventor and his dog comes from a studio in the city.

clue.text: Broad's poor delivery

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, a ... is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, penalised with an extra run

explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad' looks like the England bowler Stuart Broad, whose poor delivery would be a wide.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means extensive in width and also names an errant bowl in cricket.

clue.text: Watch loses second and minute

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a sentry keeps watch, a guard

explanation.surface: A timepiece runs slow by a second and a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute, as a noun, is a recorded note, an item in a log or record.

clue.text: Everyone can see that Carol's on drugs

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: It is obvious to all that Carol is taking narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol reads as a woman's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is said to be using, the slang sense of taking narcotics.

clue.text: See 7
Deadlines set in stone?

parts.note: deadlines read as lines for the dead, carved on a gravestone

explanation.walkthrough: Deadlines suggests fixed schedules; split as 'dead lines' they are words for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription carved on a tomb commemorating the person buried there.

clue.text: Superhero charged with identity theft essentially in torturous case?

indicators.note: charged with means filled with, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: Iron Man is the Marvel superhero
ID is the short form of identity

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the central letter of the word theft

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero is accused of stealing someone's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron maiden was a legendary torture device, a spiked cabinet enclosing its victim.

clue.text: Sweets from New York City's outskirts

parts.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here those of City, read as a phrase joining them

explanation.surface: Confectionery bought on the edge of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York City' looks like one phrase, but 'from New York' marks the American word and 'City's outskirts' are its two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American term for confectionery, which Britons call sweets.

clue.text: Trip into a plastered wall

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, so the letters are staggered into new order

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into a freshly plastered wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition is an internal dividing wall separating rooms.

clue.text: Popular song and dance by Motown regularly feature in 6A fiesta

parts.note: hot means in demand, popular
an air is a tune or song
a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word Motown

explanation.surface: Popular music and dancing from Motown are a regular part of a Bristol festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of MOTOWN: OON. The Bristol International Balloon Fiesta is held each August.
explanation.definitionFit: Hundreds of these lighter-than-air craft gather at the annual Bristol event.

clue.text: Main computer network limited by storage space

indicators.note: limited by means bounded on both sides, so the network goes inside

parts.note: an attic is a roof space used for storage
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A central computer network is constrained by lack of storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean, and the Atlantic is one, an example.

clue.text: Thieves seen around trendy side of 6A

indicators.note: seen around means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: thieves as a verb means robs
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: Burglars are spotted near a fashionable part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Thieves reads as a plural noun but is the verb. Bristol City football club are nicknamed the Robins.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belongs to the city's football team, a side in the sporting sense.

clue.text: One humped, climaxed and left

parts.note: came is a slang sense of climaxed

explanation.surface: A saucy account of a brief encounter: the deed done, the partner departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is an animal with a hump on its back, read as one that is humped.

clue.text: Cocaine hit becomes vice

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
to lamp is British slang for to hit hard

explanation.surface: A hit of cocaine turns into a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice' suggests a bad habit; it is the workshop tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp grips work tightly like a vice, the bench tool with jaws.

clue.text: Mexican snack filled with beans occasionally and this sauce?

indicators.note: filled with means the picked letters go inside the snack

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla

indicators.note: occasionally means taking alternate letters of beans, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A taco stuffed with beans, with a hot sauce on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery chilli condiment, the kind poured over Mexican food.

clue.text: 6A artist edges closer to notoriety

parts.note: banks are the edges of a river

indicators.note: closer to means the closing letter of notoriety

explanation.surface: A Bristol artist inches closer to fame and infamy.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy, the anonymous street artist, came out of Bristol's graffiti scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The pseudonymous graffiti artist is a native of the city.

clue.text: Twig circling river that's big in 6A

indicators.note: circling means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to twig is to understand, to get
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A branch lies around a river that is important in Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gert' is Bristolian dialect for big or very, as in 'gert lush'.
explanation.definitionFit: The local dialect word is an intensifier meaning large or very in the city's speech.

clue.text: Lamenting corrupt order

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grieves over a corrupt system.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is arrangement in a line, a putting into proper sequence.

clue.text: International beef from the East, Osaka namely?

indicators.note: from the East means read from right to left in an across clue

parts.note: to beef is to complain, to moan

explanation.surface: A global trade dispute from Japan, specifically involving the city of Osaka.
explanation.walkthrough: Osaka looks like the Japanese city; it is the tennis player Naomi Osaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is the first name of the tennis champion Osaka, so it is her given name.

clue.text: Man-eater's so stuck up

indicators.note: stuck up means placed upwards, read bottom to top in a down clue

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A predatory woman is snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man-eater' suggests a femme fatale; it is the fairy-tale giant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a giant in folk tales who devours humans.

clue.text: Foresee booze being knocked back in pints

indicators.note: in means the reversed drink goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for pint

indicators.note: knocked back means drunk, and also turned back, so read backwards

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink, booze

explanation.surface: A drinker sees what is coming while downing pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being knocked back' reverses CIDER to REDIC, appropriately for the West Country's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to forecast or anticipate a future event.

clue.text: Grumpy when missing out to some extent

indicators.note: missing means lacking a word, which is dropped

parts.note: out of sorts means irritable, grumpy

explanation.surface: Someone sulks when left out of something, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Of sorts is an idiom meaning after a fashion, in a loose or partial way.
